clue.text: It's brave to rise in a gas for smoking

indicators.note: in signals that the gas abbreviation is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control
a brave is a hero, a courageous warrior

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the word to is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dare to stand up in a cloud of gas, apparently something for smokers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses 'to' because this is a down clue; 'brave' is a noun here, a warrior, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheroots are cigars cut square at both ends, made to be smoked.

clue.text: Kept for breeding, not having completed academic course

indicators.note: a course not completed stops short, so the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a study is a course of academic work

explanation.surface: Someone dropped out of university and was put out to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having completed' drops the last letter of STUDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud animal is one kept specifically for breeding, as at a stud farm.

clue.text: Did he collapse after last theorem?

definitions.text: Did he collapse after last theorem?

indicators.note: collapse suggests the letters fall apart and are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A mathematician might well have collapsed after finishing his famous last theorem.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTER plus M, the last letter of 'theorem', rearranged gives the mathematician whose Last Theorem stayed unproved for 350 years.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre de Fermat is famous for the Last Theorem he claimed to have proved in a margin.

clue.text: An offence by one officer, who is an idiot

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
a sin is a moral offence
one is the Roman numeral I
CO is short for commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer who commits an offence is called a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinico is an old word, from Spanish for little donkey, meaning a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Primitive primate, born to George and Barbara?

definitions.meaning: a small nocturnal African primate of an early lineage, the galago
a child of George and Barbara Bush, the American presidential family

explanation.surface: A primitive monkey, perhaps the child of a famous American couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby or galago is a small big-eyed African primate; a Bush baby is the child of the Bush family.

clue.text: Presses to work for literary agents

definitions.meaning: presses as a verb: forces people into military service
con means to study, and agents study manuscripts

explanation.surface: Newspapers and publishing houses supposedly employing literary agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presses' looks like printing firms, but it is a verb: to press men into service. The second reading splits the word as con (study) scripts.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripts as a verb means enlists compulsorily, just as a press gang did.

clue.text: Last word by one about to put up pictures

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means the whole string is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
one is the Roman numeral I
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone getting the final word in just before hanging some pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put up' turns AMEN, I and C together to read CINEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: The pictures is an informal name for the cinema, a place to see films.

clue.text: Mad type on board goes to pieces

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so the steamship letters surround the other piece

parts.note: on board suggests a ship, and SS is a steamship
the Mad Hatter is the character from Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A deranged character on a ship falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: HATTER goes on board SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Shatters means breaks into pieces, literally or emotionally.

clue.text: "Classy" and "supreme" reflected first class place

parts.note: U means upper class, as in the U and non-U usage of the 1950s
top means best, supreme

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so this piece is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, written here with the letter I

explanation.surface: Two adjectives looking back on a first-rate spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns A1 round; the setter writes the figure 1 as the letter I. U for upper-class is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect place, named by Thomas More.

clue.text: Cockney man of fibre

indicators.note: a Cockney accent turns th into f, so the word is said as a Londoner would

parts.note: a thread is a fibre

explanation.surface: A Londoner with real strength of character.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, a working-class East Londoner, says th as f, so thread comes out as FRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred is a man's name, a short form of Frederick.

clue.text: Sea seen from Calais disturbed rest here

parts.note: the French call the English Channel La Manche

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of rest are jumbled

explanation.surface: Rough Channel waters seen from France spoil someone's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges REST. La Manche is the French name for the English Channel, literally the sleeve, so 'seen from Calais' asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Here stands for the city named, read as the place the clue points to.

clue.text: When not at work sit around, below stairs perhaps

indicators.note: around means sit is placed about the other piece

parts.note: someone off is not at work

explanation.surface: Lounging about when off duty, perhaps in the servants' quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below stairs' hints at servants' quarters but here means literally under a staircase, where a soffit is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A soffit is the underside of an architectural feature, such as the area beneath a staircase.

clue.text: Lily shows where Franciscans keep their funds

definitions.note: a plant of the lily family with chequered bell flowers

indicators.note: a friary keeping money holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Franciscan friars live in a friary
a till is where cash is held

explanation.surface: A flower reveals where monks store their money.
explanation.definitionFit: The fritillary is a bulbous plant of the lily family with chequered bell flowers.

clue.text: Sky pilot from church, who presides

parts.note: a pilot in the sky is an airman

explanation.surface: A clergyman from the church who runs the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky pilot' is slang for a chaplain, but here it is taken literally as AIRMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman is the person who presides over a meeting or board.

clue.text: It's able to flourish, growing among the rocks

indicators.note: to flourish here means the letters are waved about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something capable of thriving in a rockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flourish' rearranges ITSABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a feathery perennial grown in gardens, including rockeries.

clue.text: Poet and politician having assumed office with gravity

parts.note: Gordon Brown, British Chancellor and later Prime Minister
a party in power is said to be in
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A politician gets into office with due seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was a leading UK Labour politician, Chancellor when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning was a Victorian poet; Elizabeth Barrett Browning was another.

clue.text: Sorting my post to start Monday gives a sign of my state

indicators.note: sorting the post rearranges the letters of the two words
the start of Monday is its first letter

explanation.surface: Going through the mail on Monday reveals how I am.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorting' rearranges MYPOST to SYMPTO, and 'start' gives M from Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign of a condition, here of one's own state of health.

clue.text: It turned as 'e motored

indicators.note: turned means the letters are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something going round as a man drove along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges EMOTORED; the dropped h of 'he' is a cockney touch to supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer records the distance travelled, its wheels turning as the car is driven.

clue.text: It may be given till printed

definitions.text: It may be given till printed

parts.words: It may be given till printed
parts.note: a slip handed over at a shop, printed out by the cash register

explanation.surface: Something handed over only once it has gone to print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' reads as until, but it is the shop's cash till that prints this slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is printed by the till and given as proof of payment.

clue.text: Stupid-sounding shape to enhance the figure

indicators.note: sounding means the words are said out loud to give the answer

parts.note: silly means stupid, and said aloud it comes out like the first part of the answer
a cone is a geometric shape

explanation.surface: A daft-looking form used to improve one's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone implants are used in cosmetic surgery to enlarge the bust.

clue.text: Turn up wearing green

parts.note: in clothes means wearing them
vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: Arriving dressed in green.
explanation.definitionFit: To invert something is to turn it upside down.

clue.text: History on record is found in these letters

parts.note: history is the past

explanation.surface: A historical record kept in a collection of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Paston Letters are a famous collection of 15th-century Norfolk family correspondence, a key historical record.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paston family's letters are the best-known surviving English medieval correspondence.

clue.text: A bird reportedly coming from shell?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Shell, the oil company, sells petrol

explanation.surface: A bird that apparently hatched from a shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The shell of an egg is a false trail: Shell is the fuel company.
explanation.definitionFit: The petrel is a seabird, such as the storm petrel.

clue.text: Live freely under canvas, which is antisocial

indicators.note: freely means the letters of live move about without restraint

parts.note: camping under canvas means in a tent

explanation.surface: Living wild in a tent is frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges LIVE to EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil intent is a malicious purpose, the opposite of being sociable.

clue.text: Warning: ladies gone west!

indicators.note: gone means the letter for west is removed

parts.note: ladies are women

explanation.surface: An alarm raised because the women have disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes W (west) from WOMEN; 'gone west' looks like the idiom for lost.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or warning of what is to come.

clue.text: See description ending in stone

indicators.note: the ending of the word is kept, its opening letters cut away

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and the word describing it is episcopal

explanation.surface: A cross-reference telling the reader to look up how a gem is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a cross-reference but a bishop's see; the adjective for it is EPISCOPAL, and 'ending in' keeps its last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent gemstone, a precious stone.

clue.text: Rehearsal for a desert marathon?

definitions.meaning: a practice run-through before the real thing
a long race over arid ground would be a run in dry country

explanation.surface: A practice for a race through the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal; literally it would be a run in a dry place.

clue.text: Look a long time for these (unless you pay)

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: You wait forever for an honour unless you pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A wry hint at buying honours: peerages are seats in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerages are titles of nobility, which cynics say can be bought.
